🇲🇽🛢️ <u>PEMEX + PETROBRAS TAKE THE GULF — STATE OIL, NOT PRIVATE MAJORS</u>

Mexico's Pemex and Brazil's Petrobras have moved their energy alliance into execution: two state oil companies — not foreign private majors — jointly exploring deep (300–760 m) and ultra-deep (+760 m) waters of the Gulf of Mexico, with Brazilian technology aimed at reviving the Cantarell field in Campeche. Signed in Rio by Petrobras chief Magda Chambriard and Pemex's Juan Carlos Carpio, the deal also spans refining, petrochemicals, fertilizers and ethanol. (El Financiero)

🇲🇽🏭 <u>MEXICAN ENGINEERS BEAT HYUNDAI AND KIA IN US COURT — $11.5M</u>

A Georgia court ratified an $11.5 million settlement for 614 Mexican engineers brought to the US on TN visas by Hyundai, Kia and two contractors, then pushed into manual labor, underpaid, overworked and threatened with deportation. Payouts run from $4,100 to $16,800 each. "This is a crucial step to ensure migrant workers' rights are respected and paid fairly," said a migrant-rights advocate — a precedent for Mexican professionals working under the T-MEC.

🇲🇽🗿 <u>ZOQUE RITUAL CAVE YIELDS 179 ANCIENT PIECES IN CHIAPAS</u>

In a cave 20 meters deep near Cintalapa, Chiapas, INAH archaeologists documented 179 pre-Hispanic pieces and 13 ceremonial offerings left by the Zoque between 600 and 900 CE — jaguars, owls, and a 32-cm incense-burner handle carved with a serpent and quincunx. INAH director Joel Omar Vázquez Herrera called the sahumador "an excellent piece, very beautiful and representative of Zoque culture." Reported by a local guide in January, the site is now slated for LiDAR mapping.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>3.8 MILLION ABROAD SEE MEXICO'S ANCIENT WORLD</u>

Six INAH exhibitions of Mexican archaeology drew 3.8 million visitors across China, Spain and France — 1.5 million for "Ceiba y cosmos" alone. In Shanghai, 804 pieces spanning 3,000 years of Olmec, Teotihuacan, Maya and Mexica culture are on display, from the Mictlantecuhtli sculpture to Pakal's funerary ensemble from Palenque.

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>ADMIRAL BEHIND 'HUACHICOL FISCAL' LOCKED IN ALTIPLANO</u>

Rear Admiral Fernando Farías Laguna was jailed in the maximum-security Altiplano prison after Argentina expelled him to face Mexican justice over a fuel-smuggling network that moved contraband through ports in Tamaulipas, Baja California, Colima and Sonora. The FGR documented over 340 million pesos in losses from the first operations alone, with at least 12 ex-officials faking customs inspections to wave the fuel through.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>SINALOA GOVERNOR RETURNS AS US SMEAR COLLAPSES</u>

Rubén Rocha Moya resumed the governorship of Sinaloa after 112 days of leave — taken when US authorities named him over alleged ties to "Los Chapitos." After investigating for those same 112 days, Mexico's FGR found not a single element sustaining the accusation. "I return with my head held high," the Morena governor said.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>Mexico's Navy Pulls 16 From the Sea</u>

While Washington militarizes migration, Mexico's Navy rescued 16 people — 12 adults and 4 children — from a boat adrift off Yucatán near the port of Progreso. The Yucalpetén Naval Search and Rescue Station provided medical checks, hydration, food and shelter before handing them to immigration authorities "for the corresponding administrative procedures," all in stable health with no serious injuries.

🌊🇲🇽 <u>The Gulf of Mexico Is Running a Fever</u>

The Gulf of Mexico and Caribbean held 29-31°C through July as a marine heat wave struck Mexico's Pacific coast, Contralínea reports. Mexico's National Meteorological Service and Civil Protection now forecast 18-21 cyclones this Pacific season, threatening operations at the ports of Manzanillo and Lázaro Cárdenas and straining power generation in water-scarce regions, while Quintana Roo's reef-dependent tourism economy faces thermal stress already detected in nearby waters.
banner: GULF OF MEXICO 31°C: RECORD OCEAN HEAT

🇲🇽🏭 <u>Mexico Builds Its Own Electric Workhorse</u>

Olinia Carga — Mexico's homegrown electric cargo vehicle developed by the IPN, UNAM and TecNM — reaches the market in late 2027 at around 150,000 pesos, hauling 650 kg over 120 km on a charge from a standard wall outlet. Project director Roberto Capuano Tripp says it runs at "one-third the cost of a motocarro"; first-year output targets 10,000 units, 8,000 already committed, scaling to 50,000 a year, all built with majority Mexican capital.
